resource_modules.module_description: These modules provides a systematic understanding of GenAI's application to public sector work. Participants will learn about ten key areas where GenAI can streamline tasks and be encouraged to experiment with different platforms. The modules cover applications such as drafting content, brainstorming ideas, proofreading, summarizing information, role-playing, accelerating learning, coding, analyzing data, and more. A prompting framework with five components (Instruction, Role, Context, Format, and Example) is introduced, along with best practices for simplicity, clarity, flexibility, and efficiency. Participants will engage in hands-on exercises to refine prompts and explore techniques to enhance GenAI interactions.

Five crucial behaviors for responsible GenAI use are presented.

resource_modules.module_description: In this module, participants will explore the broader societal risks and uncertainties surrounding GenAI. The module focuses on copyright issues, deep fakes, astroturfing, and the private ownership of GenAI models. Participants will learn about the potential misuse of GenAI for deception, the challenges of identifying AI-generated content in public feedback, and the concentration of power among a few tech companies. The importance of aligning GenAI use with public values and the well-being of communities is emphasized.

course_part_description: Designed by Virginia Hamilton, this course gives participants a substantive overview of the human-centered design framework and offers opportunities to practice applying concepts from the course to your work.

resource_modules.module_description: Welcome to the Human Centered Design course. This first module introduces the concept of human-centered design - a method that prioritizes starting with people to better understand their needs and motivations, ultimately leading to innovation when combined with considerations of viability and feasibility. After this module, you will be able to demonstrate an understanding of the human-centered design process, including processes and design tools for each step.
resource_modules.module_resources:
• Universal Methods of Design By Bella Martin + Bruce Hanington: 125 Methods and approaches, organized and cataloged so you can understand methods, get references for further reading, and see case studies. It’s a great reference

  • The Field Guide to Human Centered Design The classic IDEO guide to HCD. Lots of case studies, examples, as well as How To. The Guide can be downloaded or used online

  • Observatory of Public Sector Innovation: The OECD’s innovation in government website. It says, in About Us: “Turn the new into the normal. We equip governments and public servants with fresh insights, knowledge, tools, and connections to help them explore new possibilities.” There are lots of frameworks and case studies from around the world

  • Transform with Design edited by Jochen Schwietzer, Sihem Benmahmoud-Jouni, Sebastian Fixon: Stories of how people implemented HCD in various organizations, from large corporations to health care institutions and government. (Shameless promotion: This book has a chapter about Virginia Hamilton)

  • Hack Your Bureaucracy: Get Things Done No Matter What Your Role on Any Team Marina Nitse and Nick Sinai: Not a book about HCD per se, but an important book about getting things done in a government setting, focusing on innovation and creating a modern government

  • Recoding America: Why Government Is Failing in the Digital Age and How We Can Do Better Jennifer Pahlka: A description of how government has fallen behind, the issues and problems inherent in government agencies, and examples of how innovation can happen within the constraints of bureaucracies

resource_modules.module_description: In this module, you will apply methods from the empathize process step to develop a problem statement, stakeholder map, empathy map, and journey map. After this module, you will be able to collect information from an interview to compose an empathy map, define a human-centered problem that is solution-agnostic, map stakeholders, identify customer groups for research and influential groups for relationship building, and create a journey map that illustrates a customer experience.
resource_modules.module_resources:
Problem Framing

  • What’s Your Problem? Thomas Wedell-Wedellsborg: This terrific book introduces a method for framing and reframing problems. It has many examples, activities, and visual prompts to help you ensure you are anchoring on the right problem.

  • Abstraction Ladder Luma Institute’s description of how to use the Abstraction Ladder when looking at a problem, to use various lenses before landing on the right problem. 

  • The 5 Whys A good article about the origin and ways to use the 5 Whys process.

 

Stakeholder Mapping

  • Stakeholder Mapping: The Interaction Design Foundation’s article and video about how to create and use a stakeholder map. 

  • Stakeholder Map: Civic Makers’ tool for stakeholder mapping, both available as a PDF and as a template in Mural

  • Asset Mapping UCLA Center for Health Policy Research: This is an older document (it mentions Mapquest), but very good at the hows and whys of asset mapping in a community. This is within the healthcare context and is very relevant to the government.

 

Empathy Interviews

  • Empathy FieldGuide Stanford d. school: A practical and useful guide to help you plan customer research, from empathy interviews to observation.

  • Conduct Empathy Interviews The Learning Accelerator: A well-designed guide to conducting empathy interviews, with other links and sources to explore. 

 

Journey Mapping

  • Draw Toast Tom Wujak: It's a great video to kick off a journey mapping activity. Wujak uses the process of drawing toast to describe the process of mapping a process.

resource_modules.module_description: In this module, you will demonstrate an understanding of data synthesis, including affinity mapping, and will apply methods from the define process step to develop a How Might We statement and persona.
resource_modules.module_resources:
Data Synthesis

  • How to Write Compelling User Research Insights in 6 Steps D  Scout: This is an easy-to-read (and follow) guide to moving from customer research to insights.

  • How Exactly to you find User Insights? UX Collective: This is a well-written article about how to synthesize the data you have collected in research into insights to be used for ideation.

 

HMW questions

  • Using “How Might We” Questions to Ideate on the Right Problems Neilson Norman Group:This is an excellent description of ways to develop good How Might We statements that are generative and scaled at the right level.

  • How Might We Google Design Sprint: In addition to providing advice about good How Might We questions, this is part of a larger resource for conducting Design Sprints.

 

Personas

  • Personas - Why and How you should use them. Interaction Design: This is a comprehensive website with lots of useful thinking about personas. Also look at their video.

resource_modules.module_description: In this module, you will apply methods from the ideate process step to generate and evaluate ideas and develop a concept solution. you will be able to generate different ideas to solve a problem and evaluate a set of ideas based on their customer desirability, technical feasibility, and viability. Additionally, you will be able to develop a solution concept that explains the customer, the problem addressed, how it works, assumptions made, and the next steps for implementation.
resource_modules.module_resources:
Brainstorming

  • IDEO brainstorming rules: A list of rules for brainstorming and a poster you can download to place on the wall. 

  • Protobot Molly Wilson: An amazing website that helps loosen you up for ideation. Press the Randomise button, and you will have a new invention to figure out. It's great to use before going into a brainstorming session. 


Prioritizing Solutions

  • Prioritization Matrices Neilson Norman Group: This is a good article that describes various ways of prioritizing ideas and which should be moved forward into prototyping.

resource_modules.module_description: In this module, you will demonstrate an understanding of rapid prototyping and this knowledge to prototype and test their concept with a customer. you will be able to describe the value and characteristics of rapid prototyping, create a prototyping plan for their concept, create a low-fidelity prototype of their solution, and test their low-fidelity prototype with a customer to gather feedback.
resource_modules.module_resources:

  • A Complete Introduction to Prototyping CareerFoundry: This website provides lots of advice and examples on the value and process of building prototypes and testing

course_part_description:
Course Length: 60 minutes

Learn how AI can support procurement work, from market research and solicitations to contract management, and how to manage the risks of buying and using AI in government.

resource_modules.module_resources:
Learn more

  • Responsible AI for Public Professionals (InnovateUS): A free, short course on what generative AI is and the core behaviors for using it responsibly in government.

resource_modules.module_title: Module 2: Understanding AI’s Potential for Public Procurement
resource_modules.module_resources:
Learn more

  • AI-Powered Procurement (NASPO and NASCIO): A joint brief on the main procurement AI use cases, the obstacles, and best practices for procurement and IT collaboration.

  • NASPO: Digitization and AI Are Reshaping State Procurement (StateTech): Covers NASPO’s Top 10 priorities for state procurement, where AI, analytics, and modernization rank near the top.

  • AI in Procurement Is a Game Changer for Government (StateTech): NASPO’s perspective on AI for market research and RFP support, and on why contract award decisions must stay explainable.

resource_modules.module_title: Module 3: AI Applications Across the Procurement Lifecycle
resource_modules.module_resources:
Learn more

  • AI Across the Procurement Lifecycle: Where Does It Actually Fit? (InnovateUS, Partners for Public Good, NASPO): A recorded workshop on where AI fits in planning, solicitation, evaluation, and contract management.

  • OMB Memorandum M-25-22: Driving Efficient Acquisition of AI in Government: Federal guidance organized by acquisition stage, a useful parallel to the five-stage lifecycle.

  • AI in Public Procurement (OECD): International examples of AI across the procurement lifecycle.

  • AI in Public Procurement: Between Experimentation and Impact (Open Contracting Partnership): A catalog of real government procurement AI pilots, organized by use case.

resource_modules.module_title: Module 4: Practical Applications in AI Procurement
resource_modules.module_resources:
Learn more

  • Getting Started Without Getting Overwhelmed and AI Tools Showcase (InnovateUS, Partners for Public Good, NASPO): Recorded workshops featuring Aran Raz (Westminster), Daniel Culotta (Austin), and Santiago Garcés (Boston).

  • Human in the Loop: Aran Raz on AI and Modernizing Public Procurement (The Big Bid Theory podcast): Westminster’s procurement manager on repeatable workflows and keeping AI a tool, not a liability.

  • Assistive Buyers Engine (ABE) (Burnes Center, Northeastern University): The project page for the tool built with Massachusetts OSD to help buyers navigate procurement rules.

  • AI & Cities: What Boston’s BidBot Can Teach Us About AI in Government (Harvard Kennedy School): An event on lessons from BidBot’s development and adoption.

  • 3 AI Roadblocks and How to Overcome Them (Bloomberg Cities): Includes Boston’s approach to building trust in its procurement AI tool.

  • Artificial Intelligence at the City of Austin: Governance, Training, & Strategy: Daniel Culotta’s presentation on Austin’s AI standards and governance foundation.

  • Cities Need a New Model for Incentivizing Responsible AI (Tech Policy Press): Emily Royall reflects on San Antonio’s AI pilots, including procurement tools.

Learn more

  • NIST AI Risk Management Framework and Generative AI Profile: The standard framework for structuring AI oversight and identifying risks like hallucination and data security.

  • GovAI Coalition Templates: Free, editable AI policy, incident response, vendor FactSheet, and vendor agreement templates.

  • Open the Pod Bay Doors: Navigating the Intersection of Public Records and Generative AI (MRSC): Practical guidance on treating AI prompts and outputs as public records and retaining them.

  • The Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and the Public Records Act (UNC School of Government): A plain-language explanation of why prompts and outputs can be public records.

  • Are the Government’s Conversations with AI Accessible Under Public Records Laws and FOIA? (ABA): An overview of the unsettled law on public access to government AI use.

resource_modules.module_title: Module 6: AI Implementation Strategies for Procurement Teams
resource_modules.module_resources:
Learn more

  • Building AI That Works: Implementation Strategies for Public Service (InnovateUS): A free course on choosing first projects, improving data quality, and managing risk.

  • How Cities Use the Power of Public Procurement for Responsible AI (Carnegie Endowment): Explains the GovAI Coalition’s vendor disclosure form and contract clauses for buying AI.

  • Buy AI (GSA): Practical guidance on using AI already available to you, starting from needs, and controlling costs.

  • The Powerful Tool Behind Your AI Buying Decisions (APA Planning Magazine): Emily Royall of Partners for Public Good on setting performance thresholds before signing AI contracts.

  • AI Procurement in a Box (World Economic Forum): A foundational toolkit for problem-first AI purchasing.

  • City AI Connect (Bloomberg Center for Government Excellence): A peer community with shared prompts, policies, and training materials for city staff.

resource_modules.module_title: Module 7: Strategy to Action: Building Your Procurement AI Plan
resource_modules.module_resources:
Learn more

  • Procurement Excellence Network (Partners for Public Good): A free peer network offering roundtables, templates, and coaching for procurement teams.

  • NASPO Procurement U Course Catalog: Procurement U is NASPO’s award-winning learning program and the preferred training provider for the Procurement Professionals Alliance (PPA), helping NASPO and PPA members build their skills, advance their careers, and better serve their communities.

  • From Hype to How-To: Generative AI’s Evolving Role in Procurement (Partners for Public Good): A recorded webinar on early government use cases in market research, solicitations, and contract management.

  • Taking AI Experimentation to the Next Level in Cities (Bloomberg Cities): A test-and-learn approach for moving from AI pilots to scale.

  • AI Guide for Government (GSA): A leader-focused guide to organizing for AI, starting small, and coordinating across offices.

  • Practical Approaches to Evaluating AI for Public Benefit and Worker-Centered AI Adoption in the Public Sector (InnovateUS): Free courses on measuring AI impact and bringing staff along through change.
